name: Question 10
worked_solution:
To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{e}^{2x-y}) \\  & =4{e}^{2x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-{e}^{2x-y}) \\  & ={e}^{2x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ and ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(0,1) & =4{e}^{2(0)-1}=4{e}^{-1} \\ {g}_{yy}(0,1) & ={e}^{2(0)-1}={e}^{-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xx}(0,1)\cdot {g}_{yy}(0,1)=4{e}^{-1}\cdot {e}^{-1}=4{e}^{-2}.
$$

Question 10
?

Find gxx(x,y)⋅gyy(x,y) at (0,1) given that gx(x,y)=2e2x−y and gy(x,y)=−e2x−y.

a
−e−3
b
2(e−1−e−2)
c
2e−1
d
−2e−2
e
4e−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find gxx(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative gx(x,y) with respect to x:

gxx(x,y)=∂∂x(gx(x,y))=∂∂x(2e2x−y)=4e2x−y

To find gyy(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative gy(x,y) with respect to y:

gyy(x,y)=∂∂y(gy(x,y))=∂∂y(−e2x−y)=e2x−y

Next, we evaluate gxx(x,y) and gyy(x,y) at (0,1): gxx(0,1)=4e2(0)−1=4e−1gyy(0,1)=e2(0)−1=e−1

Finally, we have

gxx(0,1)⋅gyy(0,1)=4e−1⋅e−1=4e−2.
